newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Experts says Jamuna bridge to spur economy.
newsitem.headline: Experts says Jamuna bridge to spur economy.

text.p: The Resident Representative of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) on Thursday welcomed the construction of a bridge over Bangladesh's Jamuna river, saying it would spur economic development in the country's northwest.

"The bridge will certainly boost economic activity and raise hopes for the relatively under-developed northwestern region (of Bangladesh)," Bhanuphol Horayangura told members of the Economic Reporters Forum in Dhaka.
Construction of the $700 million bridge is to be completed by October 1998. Besides being a road and rail link, the bridge will also carry a gas pipeline and power lines.
The project will be financed by the World Bank, the ADB and Japan.

K.M.S.A. Kaiser, a senior official with Bangladesh's planning department, said a study had been conducted to formulate a development plan for the country's northwestern districts after the construction of the bridge.
The study is focusing on five vital sectors -- agriculture, fisheries, industry, urban development, transport and infrastructure.
Forest Cookson, the head of the team conducting the study, said they had identified three major constraints to development in northwestern Bangladesh -- transport, energy and financing.

The study, which is due to be completed soon, points out that the northwest of Bangladesh is the poorest area of the country. Of a population of some 40 million in the north and northwest, 57.4 percent are landless, 68 percent live below the poverty line and only six percent have access to electricity.
Cookson said the 4.8 km (3 mile) bridge would help bring the country's power and gas distribution networks under a national grid. Transportation and economic growth would be speeded up.
"We have recommended establishment of an export processing zone in the area," Cookson said.
